IMRT treatment plans delivered with dynamic MLC produce a higher dose equivalent due to the production of more neutrons compared to conventional treatment plans.
IMRT delivery using 18 MV photons results in a higher neutron dose equivalent than conventional radiation therapy and the dose equivalent is proportional to the monitor unit.
the secondary neutron dose is significantly higher in IMRT than conventional radiation therapy, and the secondary neutron dose can be accurately calculated using MCNPX for a static field.

the development of methods to reduce the secondary neutron dose from IMRT treatment delivery.
the development of a Monte Carlo model of a linear accelerator treatment head and its application to the calculation of the neutron fluence from IMRT.
the measurement of the neutron fluence, neutron spectrum, and neutron effective dose for IMRT delivery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
secondary neutron doses from IMRT treatment delivery are higher than conventional treatments.
the secondary neutron dose from the delivery of IMRT treatment plans using dynamic MLC is higher than that of conventional treatment delivery.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the secondary dose from the delivery of IMRT treatment plans using dynamic MLC is higher than the conventional treatment plans.
the neutron fluence and dose equivalent are higher for IMRT than for conventional treatment.
the neutron dose equivalent for IMRT is approximately equal to the product of the monitor units and the neutron dose equivalent of conventional treatment.

secondary neutron dose should be considered in the design of future IMRT treatment plans.
the secondary neutron dose is an important component of the overall radiation dose for IMRT treatment plans.
